questions.question: Is the placement of the new code consistent with the project's existing crate and module layout?
Do fallible functions return Result with a typed error rather than panicking?
Is unwrap or expect confined to tests, prototypes, and cases proven infallible with a comment?
Do error types implement Error, Debug, and Display, with structured variants at library boundaries and a catch-all only at the binary edge?
Is the ? operator used with From conversions rather than manual match-and-return?
Are panics and error conditions documented in Panics and Errors sections?
Is behavior abstracted through a trait with the smallest useful surface, not a trait per struct?
Is static dispatch (generics, impl Trait) versus dynamic dispatch (dyn Trait) chosen deliberately, with the reason recorded?
Do public types eagerly implement the common traits that apply — Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, Send, Sync?
Are traits meant to be closed sealed against downstream implementation?
Do conversions follow the standard traits (From, Into, TryFrom, AsRef) rather than bespoke methods?
Do identifiers follow RFC 430 casing — UpperCamelCase types and traits, snake_case functions and modules, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants?
Do conversion methods follow as_, to_, into_ semantics by cost and ownership?
Do getters omit the get_ prefix, and do collections expose iter, iter_mut, into_iter?
Are names the same canonical names used elsewhere in this project for the same thing?
Are unit tests in #[cfg(test)] modules beside the code and integration tests in tests/?
Does the public API carry documentation comments with runnable examples (doc tests)?
Is the crate metadata (description, license, repository, keywords) complete for anything published?
Are iterator adapters used where they are clearer than index loops, with collect only when a collection is actually needed?
Are allocations in hot paths measured before being optimized, with a benchmark for performance-sensitive code?
Is the release profile configured deliberately (opt-level, LTO, debug symbols)?
Is shared ownership (Rc, Arc) justified by the design rather than used by default?
Is interior mutability (RefCell, Mutex, RwLock) minimal, and is each lock's scope kept short and documented?
Are reference cycles impossible or broken with Weak?
Is message passing chosen over shared state where the design allows?
Are types that cross thread boundaries Send and Sync by design, not by unsafe impl?
Is async used only where I/O-bound concurrency demands it, with compute-bound work on threads?
Is the async runtime chosen once for the project and not mixed?
Are blocking calls kept off the executor (spawn_blocking or a dedicated thread)?
Are futures that hold resources cancellation-safe, and are timeouts explicit?
Are Streams used for sequences of async values rather than hand-rolled loops over channels?
Is unsafe absent, or isolated in a minimal module with a SAFETY comment stating the invariant upheld?
Is every FFI boundary wrapped in a safe API that owns the invariants?
Is unsafe code checked under Miri?
Are macros used only where functions and generics cannot express the abstraction?
Does the change pass cargo fmt and cargo clippy with this project's lint configuration and no new warnings?
Is the toolchain pinned (rust-toolchain.toml) where reproducibility matters?
Is the code inside a module with a go.mod naming the module path, and is go.sum committed?
Is each package one directory with a short, lowercase, singular name that does not stutter with its identifiers and is not util, common, or misc?

questions.question: Are binaries under cmd/ and non-public packages under internal/, so privacy is enforced by the toolchain?
questions.sourceTerm: Organizing a Go module; internal packages

questions.question: Is the placement consistent with this project's existing module layout?
Is the go directive set deliberately, with a toolchain directive where reproducibility matters?
Is the dependency set minimal, go mod tidy clean, and govulncheck run?
questions.sourceTerm: A little copying is better than a little dependency (Go Proverbs); Vulnerability management

questions.question: Are executable tool dependencies tracked with tool directives rather than a tools file workaround?
Is all code gofmt-formatted, with imports grouped standard library first?
Are identifiers MixedCaps with consistent initialisms (URL, ID, HTTP) and no underscores?
Do getters omit the Get prefix, and do single-method interfaces end in -er?
Are receiver names short, consistent across a type's methods, and never this or self?
Does every exported identifier carry a doc comment beginning with its name, and every package a package comment?
questions.sourceTerm: Doc comments; package comments (Code Review Comments)

questions.question: Are variable names short in small scopes and descriptive in large ones?
Are names the same canonical names used elsewhere in this project for the same thing?
Are interfaces defined on the consumer side and kept to one or two methods?
questions.sourceTerm: Interfaces (Code Review Comments); The bigger the interface, the weaker the abstraction (Go Proverbs)

questions.question: Do functions accept interfaces and return concrete types?
questions.sourceTerm: Accept interfaces, return structs (Code Review Comments)

questions.question: Is composition via embedding used rather than simulated inheritance?
Is the zero value of each type useful, with a constructor only where invariants require one?
questions.sourceTerm: Make the zero value useful (Go Proverbs; Effective Go)

questions.question: Is the receiver kind (pointer or value) chosen once per type and applied to all its methods?
Where a type is intended to satisfy an interface, is a compile-time interface check present?
Are type parameters used only where they remove real duplication, with named constraints?
Is any interface{} or any justified, rather than used to avoid a type?
Is every returned error checked, never discarded with the blank identifier?
Are errors returned rather than panicked, with panic reserved for unrecoverable programmer errors?
questions.sourceTerm: Don't panic (Code Review Comments; Go Proverbs)

questions.question: Are error strings lowercase without trailing punctuation?
Are errors wrapped with %w and inspected with errors.Is or errors.As, never by string matching?
Are sentinel errors and custom error types exported deliberately as part of the API?
Is the error path handled and returned early so the happy path stays unindented?
Are in-band error values (-1, empty string, nil) replaced by a second return value?
Are named result parameters used only where they document meaning, and naked returns avoided?
questions.sourceTerm: Named result parameters; naked returns (Code Review Comments)

questions.question: Is cleanup deferred immediately after acquisition?
Are functions synchronous by default, leaving concurrency to the caller?
Are small values passed by value rather than by pointer for the sake of it?
Is context.Context the first parameter, named ctx, passed explicitly and never stored in a struct?
Are cancellation and deadlines propagated and honored (select on ctx.Done, or ctx-aware APIs)?
Are context values limited to request-scoped data and never used to pass required parameters?
Does every goroutine have a known lifetime — who stops it, when, and how it exits?
Is channel ownership clear, with the sender the only party that closes?
Is shared state either protected by a mutex or avoided by passing data over channels?
questions.sourceTerm: Share memory by communicating; channels orchestrate, mutexes serialize (Go Proverbs; Effective Go)

questions.question: Are goroutines coordinated with sync.WaitGroup (WaitGroup.Go) or errgroup, never time.Sleep?
Is go test -race part of the test run?
Is any leftover loop-variable capture workaround removed now that loop variables are per-iteration?
Is concurrency introduced for a measured reason, not by default?
Is slice and map aliasing understood, with copies made deliberately where the caller may mutate?
Are empty slices declared as var s []T rather than []T{} unless a non-nil value is required (JSON)?
Is make used to preallocate where the size is known?
Are time.Time and time.Duration used for time, never bare integers?
Are sequences exposed as iterators (iter.Seq) where range-over-func fits?
Are tests table-driven with t.Run subtests, in _test.go files beside the code?
Do failures report got and want with context via t.Errorf, not panics?
Are testable Examples provided for exported API?
Are benchmarks present for performance-sensitive code and fuzz tests where input is parsed?
Is coverage measured against this project's threshold?
Do go vet and this project's linter pass, and has go fix been run for modernizers?
Is logging structured with log/slog rather than fmt.Println or the legacy log package?
Is an HTTP server built on net/http with routing patterns and explicit timeouts before a framework is reached for?
Is the binary static where deployment expects one file (CGO_ENABLED=0 when cgo is not needed)?
Do route files use the App Router file conventions (layout, page, loading, error, not-found, route) rather than ad-hoc names?
Is non-route code colocated in private folders or outside app, and are route groups used only for organization and shared layouts?
questions.sourceTerm: Route groups; private folders; colocation (Project Structure)

questions.question: Is the placement consistent with this project's existing structure (app, ui or components, lib)?
Are secrets only in server-side environment variables, with NEXT_PUBLIC_ reserved for values that are safe to ship to the browser?
Are module path aliases used instead of deep relative imports?
Is shared UI in a layout and page-specific UI in a page, with exactly one root layout?
questions.sourceTerm: Root layout; nested layouts (Layouts and Pages)

questions.question: Are internal links rendered with the Link component so prefetching and client-side navigation apply?
Are params and searchParams awaited and typed for dynamic segments?
Are redirects performed with redirect on the server rather than client-side effects where possible?
Is 'use client' applied only where interactivity or browser APIs are required, at the leaves of the tree?
Are all props crossing the server-to-client boundary serializable?
Are server-only modules (database client, secrets) never imported into Client Components, with server-only marking where it matters?
Are Server Components passed into Client Components as children rather than imported by them?
Is data fetched in Server Components (or through Route Handlers for client consumers), not in client effects by default?
Is slow or non-critical data wrapped in Suspense or loading.js so the shell streams?
Are independent requests fetched in parallel rather than as a sequential waterfall?
Is database access isolated in a data layer (lib/data) rather than inline in components?
questions.sourceTerm: Data Access Layer (Authentication guide; Foundations course)

questions.question: Are mutations implemented as Server Functions or Server Actions under 'use server' rather than client-side fetches to hand-rolled endpoints?
Does every Server Function validate its input and check authorization server-side, since it is a public endpoint?
questions.sourceTerm: Input validation; authorization (Mutating Data; ASVS V4)

questions.question: After a mutation, is the affected cache revalidated with revalidatePath or revalidateTag before redirecting?
Are pending and error states surfaced with useActionState or useFormStatus?
Is the caching strategy for each route and data source explicit (static, dynamic, or Cache Components with 'use cache') rather than assumed from defaults?
Is revalidation chosen deliberately — time-based or on-demand — and are cache tags named canonically?
Is user-specific or session-specific data excluded from shared caches?
Are expected errors returned as values to the UI, and only uncaught exceptions left to error.js boundaries?
Is not-found handled with notFound and a not-found.js at the right segment?
Is a global-error.js present to catch root layout failures?
Is styling done with this project's chosen method (Tailwind or CSS Modules) rather than mixed ad hoc?
Are images rendered with next/image with dimensions or fill and sizes set?
Are fonts loaded with next/font rather than external stylesheet links?
Is metadata defined through the Metadata API — static or generateMetadata — including Open Graph images for public pages?
Are sitemap and robots generated through the file conventions where the site is public?
Is a Route Handler used only where a Server Function does not fit (webhooks, external clients), with correct HTTP method exports and Web Response objects?
Is Proxy limited to rewrites, redirects, headers, and optimistic checks — never the sole authorization gate?
Is authorization enforced in the Data Access Layer next to the data it protects?
Is the deployment target (Vercel, self-hosted Node, static export) chosen, and are the features used supported on that target?
Is the Next.js version current or pinned deliberately, with upgrade codemods applied when moving?
Does the plan honor the React Foundations prerequisite — components, props, state, hooks, Suspense — before introducing Server Component patterns?
Is each component a pure function of its props and state, with no side effects during render?
questions.sourceTerm: Keeping Components Pure (Learn); Rules of React

questions.question: Does the component tree map to a UI hierarchy identified before coding, with a static version buildable first?
Is each component small enough to name by one responsibility, and exported consistently with this project's convention?
Are list items keyed by stable, unique data identifiers — never the array index when items can reorder or be inserted?
Is conditional rendering expressed in JSX (ternary, &&, or early return of null) rather than imperative branches building markup?
Are props treated as read-only, with children used for composition rather than render-prop workarounds?
Are event handlers passed as functions and named handleX on the component, onX on the prop?
Is state reserved for values that change over time and drive rendering, with derived values computed during render?
questions.sourceTerm: State: A Component's Memory; Choosing the State Structure

questions.question: Are state updates treated as snapshots, using an updater function whenever the next value depends on the previous?
questions.sourceTerm: State as a Snapshot; Queueing a Series of State Updates

questions.question: Are objects and arrays in state replaced immutably, never mutated in place?
questions.sourceTerm: Updating Objects in State; Updating Arrays in State

questions.question: Is the state structure minimal — no redundant, duplicated, contradictory, or deeply nested state?
questions.sourceTerm: Choosing the State Structure; Thinking in React, step 3

questions.question: Is shared state lifted to the closest common parent, and otherwise kept local?
questions.sourceTerm: Sharing State Between Components; Thinking in React, step 4

questions.question: Where a component must reset, is the reset done with a key change rather than an Effect?
Are many related state transitions consolidated in a reducer rather than scattered across setters?

questions.question: Is Context used only for data needed deep in the tree (theme, current user, locale), not to avoid passing a prop one level?

questions.sourceTerm: Scaling Up with Reducer and Context

questions.question: Does data flow down through props and up through callbacks, with no hidden channels?

questions.sourceTerm: Lifecycle of Reactive Effects; Removing Effect Dependencies

questions.question: Does every Effect that subscribes, connects, or starts something return a cleanup?
Are non-reactive reads inside Effects separated with useEffectEvent?
Are refs used only for values that do not affect rendering and for DOM access, never read or written during render?
questions.sourceTerm: Referencing Values with Refs; Manipulating the DOM with Refs

questions.question: Is reusable stateful logic extracted into a custom Hook named useX, with a clear input and return contract?
Are Hooks called only at the top level of a component or custom Hook, never conditionally or in loops?
Are components and Hooks idempotent, so double-invocation under StrictMode produces the same result?
questions.sourceTerm: Components and Hooks must be pure; StrictMode

questions.question: Are props, state, and Hook return values never mutated?
Is StrictMode enabled at the root in development?
Is data fetched through the framework or a Suspense-enabled data library rather than raw useEffect plus fetch?
questions.sourceTerm: You Might Not Need an Effect; Suspense

questions.question: Are form submissions implemented as Actions with useActionState and useFormStatus, surfacing pending and error state?
Is optimistic UI implemented with useOptimistic where perceived latency matters?
Is the use API used to read promises or Context in render where it simplifies the code, and never called conditionally?
Are Suspense boundaries placed around slow subtrees with fallbacks at the level the design intends?
Are non-urgent updates wrapped in transitions to keep input responsive?
Is ref passed as an ordinary prop, with forwardRef removed?
Are generated ids for accessibility attributes produced with useId, never Math.random?
Is the React Compiler enabled; and if not, is manual memoization (memo, useMemo, useCallback) added only after profiling shows a need?
Is hidden-but-preserved UI implemented with Activity rather than conditional unmounting where state must survive?
Are long lists virtualized, and are large components split so a keystroke does not re-render the page?
questions.sourceTerm: Render and Commit; community best practice

questions.question: Are semantic elements, labels, keyboard operability, and ARIA used per the Authoring Practices Guide rather than div-and-onClick?
Are error boundaries placed around risky subtrees so one failure does not blank the app?
Was the project created with a framework or Vite per current guidance, never Create React App?
questions.sourceTerm: Creating a React App (CRA sunset, February 2025)

questions.question: Is eslint-plugin-react-hooks active (rules-of-hooks, exhaustive-deps) together with the compiler's lint rules?
Is React pinned at a current 19.x release, with the react-server-dom security advisories accounted for?
Is the placement consistent with this project's existing component and feature structure?
Are component props typed as interfaces where the project uses TypeScript?
Do tests query by role, label, and text rather than implementation details?
Is strict enabled, with this project's additional strictness flags (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride) applied consistently?
Do module and moduleResolution match the runtime or bundler (nodenext, bundler), with verbatimModuleSyntax on?
Is type-checking run as tsc --noEmit in CI, separate from the bundler's transpile, so transpile-only tools cannot hide type errors?
In a multi-package repository, are project references used with a single root configuration?
Is TypeScript on a current 7.x release, with any tool that imports the compiler as a library moved to @typescript/typescript6 or an updated version?
If Node executes .ts files directly, is erasableSyntaxOnly enabled — no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties?
Is any absent, with unknown plus narrowing at every boundary where the type is not known?
questions.sourceTerm: any; unknown (Everyday Types; Do's and Don'ts)

questions.question: Are the wrapper types Number, String, Boolean, Object, and the bare Function type never used?
Are unions of string literals preferred over enums; where enums remain, is that a recorded project decision?
Are null and undefined handled explicitly with optional chaining and nullish coalescing, with no non-null assertions outside a commented boundary?
Are type assertions confined to boundaries the compiler cannot see, and is satisfies used to check a value without widening it?
Are tuples and as const used where positional or literal structure matters?
Are unions narrowed with typeof, instanceof, in, and discriminant checks rather than assertions?
Do discriminated unions carry a literal discriminant, with exhaustiveness enforced through never in the default branch?
Are custom guards written as type predicates, relying on inferred predicates where 5.5+ allows?
Are parameter and return types explicit on exported functions and inferred inside modules?
Are overloads avoided where a union parameter or optional parameter suffices, and ordered specific-to-general where kept?
Is void the return type of callbacks whose result is ignored?
Are promises always awaited or returned, with catch variables typed unknown?
Is interface versus type alias chosen per this project's convention and applied consistently?
Are readonly properties and Readonly applied to data that must not be mutated?
Is a generic introduced only when a type relationship must be preserved, with a constraint and a meaningful name?
Are utility types used instead of hand-duplicated shapes derived from an existing type?
Are mapped, conditional, and template literal types used only where they remove duplication, with a comment stating the derivation?
Is a const type parameter used where a literal must be preserved through a generic call?
Are classes used only where identity, encapsulated state, or lifecycle justify them, with plain objects and functions otherwise?
Is structural compatibility understood, with branded types where nominal identity is genuinely required?
Are ES modules used with import type for type-only imports and no namespaces?
Are barrel files used deliberately, with circular imports checked?
Are tsconfig path aliases mirrored in the bundler and runtime configuration?
Do third-party types come from @types or bundled declarations, with local gaps filled by a declared .d.ts rather than any?
Does a published library emit declarations (declaration, isolatedDeclarations)?
Is every value crossing a runtime edge — JSON.parse, HTTP response, environment variable, IPC message, form data — validated with a schema, with the static type derived from the schema?
Are environment variables typed through a validated config module rather than read as any?

Where types are generated from another stack (Specta, ts-rs, typeshare, openapi-typescript, protobuf, GraphQL codegen), is the source stack the single source of truth, and is the .ts output never hand-edited?
questions.sourceTerm: Contract boundary; single source of truth

questions.question: Are generated files marked as generated, excluded from lint and formatting, and regenerated in the build so that drift fails CI?
Is the contract versioned so a source-type change surfaces as a visible boundary change on the TypeScript side?
Is the IPC or HTTP edge still runtime-validated, since generated types are erased like any other?
questions.sourceTerm: Type erasure at the contract edge

questions.question: Do generated type names match the source stack's canonical names under the codegen tool's casing rule?
Is typescript-eslint active with the type-checked rule set — no-explicit-any, no-floating-promises, consistent-type-imports?
Are @ts-ignore comments absent, with @ts-expect-error used only with a stated reason?
Is the placement consistent with this project's existing structure?
Are names the same canonical names used elsewhere in this project for the same thing?
Are variables declared with const by default and let only when reassigned, never var?
Is strict equality used, with coercion and sameness semantics understood where loose comparison appears?
Does the code run as a module (type="module", or "type": "module" in Node), so strict mode is on and nothing leaks into global scope?
Is this binding handled deliberately — arrow functions for lexical this, bound or wrapped methods when passed as callbacks?
Are template literals, destructuring, optional chaining, and nullish coalescing used for clarity rather than concatenation and nested guards?
Are dates and times handled with Temporal or explicit time-zone-aware formatting via Intl, never Date arithmetic?
questions.sourceTerm: Representing dates and times (MDN Guide); ECMA-402

questions.question: Is floating-point handled deliberately — Math.sumPrecise for sums, integer arithmetic or BigInt where exactness matters?
Is the collection chosen for the access pattern — Array for ordered lists, Map and Set for keyed or unique data, plain objects for fixed-shape records — with getOrInsert for the upsert pattern?
questions.sourceTerm: Indexed collections; Keyed collections (MDN Guide); ES2026

questions.question: Is shared data treated immutably — spread, toSorted, toReversed, with, structuredClone — rather than mutated in place?
Are classes used only where identity or prototype semantics are needed, with private fields for encapsulation and composition preferred over deep inheritance?
Are iterators and generators used for lazy sequences, with Iterator helpers instead of intermediate arrays?
Is asynchronous work written with async and await, and is every promise awaited, returned, or explicitly handled?
questions.sourceTerm: Asynchronous JavaScript: promises, async and await (MDN)

questions.question: Are errors caught at the boundary, chained with cause, and identified with Error.isError rather than instanceof across realms?
questions.sourceTerm: Control flow and error handling (MDN Guide); ES2022, ES2026

questions.question: Are independent asynchronous operations run in parallel with Promise.all or allSettled rather than awaited in sequence?
Is CPU-heavy or long-running work moved to a Web Worker or worker_threads so the main thread stays responsive?
Is cancellation implemented with AbortController for fetch, listeners, and timers?
Is deterministic cleanup done with try/finally or using declarations?
Are DOM references queried once and cached, and are DOM writes batched or built in a DocumentFragment to avoid layout thrash?
Are listeners attached with addEventListener, removed when no longer needed, and delegated to a parent for dynamic lists?
Is form submission intercepted with preventDefault only where the page must not reload, and does the form still function without JavaScript where feasible?
Is untrusted content inserted with textContent or createElement, never innerHTML?
questions.sourceTerm: Security and privacy (MDN Curriculum); ASVS V3

questions.question: Are reusable UI pieces built as Web Components — custom elements, shadow DOM, template — rather than a framework added for one widget?
questions.sourceTerm: Web Components (W3C; MDN Client-side web APIs)

questions.question: Are observers (Mutation, Intersection, Resize) used instead of polling, and disconnected when done?
Are ES modules used with explicit imports and exports, bare specifiers resolved by an import map or bundler, and no shared globals between scripts?
questions.sourceTerm: JavaScript modules (MDN Guide); import maps (WHATWG HTML)

questions.question: Is the module graph free of circular dependencies, with one responsibility per module?
Does the standard library cover the need before a dependency is added — Temporal over a date library, Uint8Array base64 methods over a polyfill, Iterator helpers over a utility library?
Are dependencies minimal, pinned by lockfile, and audited?
Is the placement consistent with this project's existing structure?
Is fetch used with response.ok checked, a timeout via AbortSignal.timeout, and JSON parsing wrapped in error handling?
questions.sourceTerm: Network requests; Fetching data (MDN); Fetch standard

questions.question: Is data arriving from JSON, URLs, or storage validated for shape before use?

Is client-side storage chosen deliberately — localStorage for small synchronous values, IndexedDB for structured or large data, cookies only for what the server needs — with quota and failure handled?
Is every web feature checked against Web Platform Baseline or this project's browserslist before use, with polyfills only where the target requires them?
questions.sourceTerm: Baseline (web.dev); Web standards and semantics (MDN Curriculum)

questions.question: Is feature detection used rather than user-agent sniffing?
Is the runtime target explicit — browser, Node 24 LTS (26 when it enters LTS), or both — and is the code free of the other runtime's globals?
Is a Content Security Policy in place, with no inline scripts and no eval or new Function?
Are DOM XSS sinks — innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, javascript: URLs — avoided, or guarded by Trusted Types or the Sanitizer API?
questions.sourceTerm: DOM sinks; Trusted Types; ASVS V3, V1

questions.question: Are tokens and secrets kept out of client code and out of localStorage where an HttpOnly cookie serves?
questions.sourceTerm: Security and privacy (MDN Curriculum); ASVS V3

questions.question: Are third-party scripts loaded with Subresource Integrity and reviewed for the permissions they take?
Are native semantic elements used before ARIA, with ARIA only where no native element exists?
questions.sourceTerm: First rule of ARIA use (W3C); Accessibility (MDN core module)

questions.question: Is every interactive element keyboard operable with visible focus, and is dynamic content announced through live regions where needed?
questions.sourceTerm: Accessibility (MDN); WCAG 2.2; ARIA Authoring Practices Guide

questions.question: Is script loading non-blocking (module or defer), split by route, and is bundle size measured?
Are Core Web Vitals measured, with long tasks broken up using scheduler.yield or requestAnimationFrame?
Are timers, intervals, listeners, and observers released so nothing leaks across navigations or component lifetimes?
Are unit tests present (node:test or this project's runner) and end-to-end tests for critical flows?
Are console.log statements removed, with structured error reporting in their place?
Does the code pass ESLint recommended rules plus this project's rules, and Prettier?
Are exported functions documented with JSDoc types where TypeScript is not in use, so editors can type-check?
Are names the same canonical names used elsewhere in this project for the same thing?

questions.section: Node.js (fires when the runtime target is Node)
questions.question: Are built-in modules imported with the node: prefix, and are promise-based APIs (fs/promises) used over callbacks and sync calls on hot paths?

questions.section: Node.js (fires when the runtime target is Node)
questions.question: Are unhandled rejections and process signals handled for graceful shutdown?

questions.section: Node.js (fires when the runtime target is Node)
questions.question: If .ts files run directly under Node, is only erasable syntax used?

questions.section: Node.js (fires when the runtime target is Node)
questions.question: Is the Node version pinned to Active LTS in package.json engines and CI?

banks.title: Domain Boundaries — user, admin, chat, AI (Draft v0.1)

questions.question: Are identity (who the subject is), authentication (proving it), and authorization (what they may do) separated in the design?
questions.sourceTerm: Digital identity model (800-63-4); ASVS V6, V8

questions.question: Is the authenticator type and its assurance level (AAL) chosen deliberately and documented?
Are memorized secrets stored with an approved hashing method and checked against known-compromised lists?
Is multi-factor or phishing-resistant authentication available where the risk requires it?
Are syncable authenticators (passkeys) supported or explicitly deferred with a reason?
Is a new session token generated on authentication, with sufficient entropy?
Are sessions invalidated on logout and bounded by idle and absolute timeouts?
questions.sourceTerm: Session logout and timeout (ASVS V7.3; AC-12)

questions.question: Are cookie-based sessions set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite?
Is re-authentication required before sensitive account changes (email, password, authenticator)?
Are unsuccessful login attempts limited and monitored?
Is account recovery treated as an authentication event with its own assurance, not a bypass?
Is the account lifecycle defined — creation, disable, removal, inactivity?
If federated login is used, are assertions validated and the FAL documented?
Are self-contained tokens validated for signature, issuer, audience, and expiry?
Is authorization enforced server-side at function, data, and field level?
Are changes to the values authorization decisions depend on applied immediately?
Is personal data in identity records minimized and its retention defined?
Are authentication and authorization failures logged as security events?
Is the administrative surface separated from the end-user surface (route, deployment, or process)?
Are administrative roles defined explicitly with non-overlapping duties?
questions.sourceTerm: Role-based access control; separation of duties (AC-3(7), AC-5; INCITS 359)

questions.question: Does each administrative role hold only the functions it needs?
Are privileged accounts distinct from the same person's ordinary account?
Is every privileged action audit-logged with actor, target, time, and outcome?
questions.sourceTerm: Log use of privileged functions (AC-6(9); AU)

questions.question: Are audit records protected from modification by the administrators they record?
Do destructive or irreversible administrative actions require confirmation or a second approver?
Is there an audited break-glass or override path rather than an undocumented one?
Are privileges reviewed periodically and is revocation applied immediately?
questions.sourceTerm: Review of user privileges; revocation (AC-6(7), AC-3(8); ASVS V8)

questions.question: Are shared or group administrative accounts prohibited?
In a multi-tenant system, is tenant isolation enforced on every administrative query?
Is system configuration changed through a controlled, versioned path rather than live edits?
Is impersonation ("log in as user") logged, consented where required, and time-bounded?
Are administrative sessions shorter-lived and re-authenticated for sensitive functions?
Do bulk operations carry scope and rate limits?
Is content moderation separated from account administration as a distinct role?
Is the delivery guarantee (at-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once) chosen and documented?
Does every message carry a client-generated idempotency key so retries do not duplicate?
Is ordering within a conversation defined (sequence number or logical clock) and enforced on display?
Is a message durably persisted before it is acknowledged to the sender?
Is the transport chosen deliberately (WebSocket, SSE, polling) with reconnect and resume from a last-seen cursor?
Is the WebSocket connection authenticated, with the token re-validated on reconnect?
Is authorization checked per message and per channel membership, not only at connect?
Is presence (online, typing) modelled as ephemeral state separate from durable messages?
Is backpressure or rate limiting applied per connection and per user?
Is fan-out to group members bounded and asynchronous?
Are retention, deletion, and "delete for everyone" semantics defined?
Are attachments handled through the file-handling boundary rather than inline in the message model?
Is message content sanitized before rendering?
Is there a report and moderation path with an audit record?
If end-to-end encryption is claimed, is the key model documented and the server unable to read content?
Are offline delivery (queue while disconnected) and read-receipt semantics defined?
Is the conversation model (one-to-one, group, channel, thread) chosen once and named canonically?
Is the model provider behind an adapter so the provider or model can change without touching callers?
questions.sourceTerm: Separation of interface and implementation (SWEBOK); Supply chain (LLM03)

questions.question: Is untrusted content (user input, retrieved documents, tool output) kept distinct from instructions when the prompt is assembled?
Is model output treated as untrusted data before it is rendered, executed, or stored?
Is the system prompt free of secrets and not relied on as a security control?
Are the tools the model can call minimal in functionality, permission, and autonomy?
Do consequential actions require human confirmation before execution?
Is sensitive data filtered before it enters the prompt and before output is returned?
Are retrieval sources access-controlled so a user cannot retrieve documents they may not read?
Are token, request, and cost budgets enforced per user and per tenant?
Are prompts versioned and tested against an evaluation set before release?
Is there a regression harness with defined quality metrics?
Are model, provider, and prompt version recorded per request?
Is there a fallback or degraded mode when the provider fails or times out?
Is training or fine-tuning data provenance recorded and separated from user data?
Is AI-generated output labelled where required, with known limitations disclosed?
Are third-party models, plugins, and embedding models pinned and verified?
Are retention and secondary use of prompts and completions defined and disclosed?
Does "train it on my data" resolve to retrieval unless fine-tuning is explicitly justified?
